text: $BTC trades near $86k after a Sunday rally lifted the weekly close about 2% higher. Derivatives positioning eased back into its normal range and ETF inflows cooled, while on-chain activity, new capital and profit-taking all run hot. https://glassno.de/4zctuPd

Whales have stopped sending $BTC to exchanges. Their summer run of net deposits lasted over three months, twice as long as any other since 2023. It ended in late August, and the flow has stayed negative since.

$BTC's largest overhead liquidation cluster sits near $90k. If price touches this level, leveraged shorts will be forced to close their positions. Zoom into the last two months and smaller clusters can be seen around $83k and $75k. Either side could speed up the next move.

$BTC long-term holders stayed in profit this entire cycle. No bear market since at least 2015 has done that. In each prior bear, LTH-MVRV fell below 1 at the cycle low, putting the cohort underwater. This time it bottomed above 1 and is now climbing again.
The market repriced the odds of an October Fed hike from 66% to 22% this week. Here is our commentary on the repricing as it happened and what Bitcoin did. https://glassno.de/pricing-out-the-hike

$BTC investors that bought the top are currently selling. Two cohorts sit underwater: buyers from 1–2 years ago at $97k, and from 6–12 months ago at $89k. Those who bought the 2025 rally are selling the most coins per day this year. Those who bought the decline are not.
